chunks: 2593 - Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Beware of boasting, and hold fast to a scrupulous piety that restrains you from acts of disobedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
For indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Then let them complete their prescribed duties."
And among the tafath is that you speak foul words during your ihram; so when you enter Makkah and perform tawaf around the House, you speak good words.
And that would be an atonement for that."

key_terms.إِحْرَامِكَ: your state of ihram during pilgrimage consecration
key_terms.بِوَرَعٍ: with scrupulous piety that keeps one away from sin
key_terms.تَفَثَهُمْ: their ritual untidiness or prescribed post-ritual completion duties in the hajj context

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about foul speech and boasting during ihram in hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs the pilgrim to avoid boasting and foul speech, especially in the state of ihram, and to adopt waraʿ that prevents disobedience to Allah. It connects the Qur'anic phrase about completing tafath with conduct during hajj, indicating that good speech after entering Makkah and performing tawaf serves as expiation for earlier improper speech.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2593 - Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
"Avoid boasting, and adhere to piety that restrains you from disobedience to Allah (swt), the Almighty.
Indeed, Allah (swt), the Almighty, says: 'Then let them complete their prescribed duties.'
Among these duties is refraining from speaking foul words while in Ihram. When you enter Makkah and perform Tawaf around the Ka'bah, speak good and kind words,
as this will serve as atonement for any inappropriate speech during your state of Ihram."
